name: Anchovy
description: As an oily fish, their strong flavour is used to add a kick to many dishes and sauces. They are small green fish with a silver stripe that gives them a bluish hue.

name: Arctic Char
description: Land based farmed Arctic char is a good choice when looking for an oily fish.

name: Basa / Vietnamese Catfish
description: This farmed species natural habitat is medium to large rivers in Asian countries such as Vietnam, where they can grow up to 44kg.

name: Seabass
description: The combination of slow growth, late maturity, spawning aggregation, and strong summer site fidelity make it vulnerable to over-exploitation.

name: Black Bream
description: Seabream are a group of compact, medium-sized fishes known as Sparidae. Their firm white meat is ideal for grilling, steaming, baking and pan-frying whole.

name: Gilthead Bream
description: A compact, medium-sized fish. Their firm white meat is similar in taste and texture to bass.

name: Brill
description: Brill is mainly landed as bycatch in beam trawl fisheries for plaice and sole, particularly in the North Sea.

name: Atlantic Cod
description: There are many different Atlantic cod populations and whilst some are being well managed and are in a healthy state, many others are in a poor state, particularly around the UK.

name: Pacific Cod
description: Choose Pacific Cod caught in Alaska. Their stocks are generally healthy and managed by a suite of management measures.

name: Coley / Saithe
description: Coley or saithe is generally a good choice. Stocks are not overfished, and are not subject to overfishing except in the Faroe Islands.

name: Dab
description: A versatile fish, dab can be grilled, baked or pan-fried whole, whilst fillets can be poached.

name: Giant Devil Ray
description: Classified as Endangered by the IUCN. They grow slowly, mature at a late age and produce very few young.

name: Lesser Spotted Dogfish
description: A small shark species common in British waters. Populations have been increasing over time.

name: Conger Eel
description: Conger eels are very susceptible to fishing pressure. Avoid eating.

name: European Eel
description: European eel populations are at an all time low. Their status remains critical and assessed as Critically Endangered in the wild.

name: Flounder
description: There are no targeted fisheries for flounder, they are taken as by-catch in trawl nets. Stocks appear to be increasing.

name: Grouper
description: Largely overfished; assessed as vulnerable to highly vulnerable to overfishing; not managed.

name: Guitarfish
description: Guitarfish are listed by IUCN as Endangered. Its biology and inshore habitat make it highly susceptible to population depletion.

name: Grey Gurnard
description: Gurnards belong to a family of fish known as 'sea robins'. It lives on the seabed and stirs up food with its 'legs'.

name: Red Gurnard
description: A fast growing fish that matures early at a large size. Gurnards are non-quota species and often discarded due to low market demand.

name: Tub Gurnard
description: The largest European gurnard, distinguished by their stunningly coloured, brilliant blue fins.

name: Haddock
description: Haddock from Irish Sea, Rockall, Northeast Arctic and Iceland are at healthy or sustainable levels.

name: Cape Hake
description: Hake has a mild flavour with a medium but firm textured meat. The Cape hake fishery has been certified as responsible by the MSC since 2004.

name: European Hake
description: The biomass for the northern stock has recovered from depleted levels and is now at a record high.

name: Atlantic Halibut
description: Atlantic halibut can grow up to 8ft long and 4ft wide and is the largest and longest lived of all flatfish. Heavily overfished and listed as Endangered.

name: Greenland Halibut
description: A long-lived, slow-growing species, making it vulnerable to exploitation, but their populations appear to be healthy.

name: Pacific Halibut
description: Pacific halibut stocks are well managed by the International Pacific Halibut Commission who apply strict harvesting conditions.

name: Herring
description: Herring is caught in large fisheries using methods that are relatively selective and non-damaging to the seabed. They have a very important role in the marine ecosystem.

name: John Dory
description: Very little is known about John dory. It is mainly caught as bycatch in hake, anglerfish and megrim fisheries.

name: Ling
description: Ling is found in both shallow coastal waters and the deep sea. More resilient to fishing than other deep-water species but vulnerable in deep water.

name: Mackerel
description: Handline-caught mackerel from the southwest of England remains the best choice. The mackerel stock in the North-East Atlantic is in a good state.

name: Blue Marlin
description: Atlantic blue marlin has been overfished for many years and is still below safe levels. Best avoided for now.

name: Meagre
description: Farmed meagre is emerging into the UK market, farmed mainly in Mediterranean countries, mainly in Italy.

name: Megrim
description: Best choice is megrim otter trawled from the Northern North Sea and West of Scotland or Rockall where stocks are assessed as healthy.

name: Monkfish / Anglerfish
description: Monkfish are long-lived and late maturing, making them vulnerable to fishing. Gillnet caught fish tend to be larger and more likely to be mature.

name: Grey Mullet
description: A thicklip mullet found in European coastal waters.

name: Red Mullet
description: There is no assessment or management of red mullet stocks. A minimum landing size of 15 cm is enforced by the Cornish IFCA.

name: Nursehound / Bull Huss
description: A shark species inherently vulnerable to overexploitation due to slow-growing, late to mature and producing few young.

name: Parrotfish
description: Parrotfish are moderately resilient to fishing but there is very little data available on their abundance or exploitation rates.

name: Plaice
description: Plaice is a popular fish for consumption and is subject to high fishing pressure. Best choices are from the North Sea or Eastern Channel.

name: Pollack
description: Insufficient information available to evaluate stock biomass. The best choice is handline-caught pollack from the southwest.

name: Alaska Pollock
description: A white fish, mild in flavour and low in fat. Makes great fishcakes and is the fish used in McDonald's Filet-O-Fish!

name: Pouting / Bib
description: A short-lived species common in British inshore waters. It is not commercially fished and is usually only taken as bycatch.

name: Blonde Ray
description: Skates and rays are vulnerable to overfishing because they grow really slowly, mature late in life and produce few young.

name: Cuckoo Ray
description: A smaller ray species found in northern European seas. Slow growing and vulnerable to overfishing.

name: Sandy Ray
description: An uncommon ray species found in deep waters around the British Isles.

name: Shagreen Ray
description: A ray species with a rough skin texture. Slow growing and vulnerable to overfishing.

name: Smalleyed Ray
description: Found mainly in shallow coastal waters. Vulnerable to overfishing due to slow growth and late maturity.

name: Spotted Ray
description: A fast-growing ray species with healthier populations than many other rays. Best choice when selecting ray to eat.

name: Starry Ray
description: A deep-water ray species. Slow growing and vulnerable to overfishing.

name: Thornback Ray
description: One of the most common rays in British waters. Slow to grow and breed, making them vulnerable to overfishing.

name: Undulate Ray
description: A ray species with distinctive wavy lines on its back. Vulnerable to overfishing.

name: Atlantic Salmon
description: Generally stocks of wild Atlantic salmon are depleted. Salmon is now widely available thanks to fish farming.

name: Chinook Salmon
description: The Chinook is the most highly prized and expensive of the Pacific salmon from the culinary perspective.

name: Chum Salmon
description: The flesh of Chum salmon is typically lighter in colour and lower in oil content than other Pacific salmon.

name: Coho Salmon
description: The Coho is considered as one of the best tasting salmon. It has a higher oil content than Pink and Chum.

name: Pink Salmon
description: Pacific salmon are a shorter lived species and much more prolific breeders than Atlantic salmon.

name: Sockeye Salmon
description: One of the five species of Pacific salmon. MSC certified Pacific salmon is the most sustainable choice.

name: Sardine / Pilchard
description: Same fish - different name depending on size. They are oily fish with bright silver skins, rich in omega-3 fatty acids.

name: Sawfish
latin_name: Pristis pristis; P. pectinata; P. perotteti
description: Sawfishes are arguably the most imperiled fishes in the world; classified as Critically Endangered by the IUCN.

name: Horse Mackerel / Scad
description: This mackerel can be smoked, fried, salted and baked. Avoid eating immature fish below about 25 cm.

name: Angel Shark
description: Angel shark is an EU Prohibited Species and Critically Endangered. Catches are now rare.

name: Blue Shark
description: Blue shark are a red-rated species. Avoid eating Blue shark.

name: Porbeagle Shark
description: Porbeagle is assessed as Critically Endangered in Northeast Atlantic by the IUCN.

name: Tope Shark
description: Tope is considered highly vulnerable to over-exploitation because they are slow-growing and long-lived.

name: Common Skate
description: EU Prohibited Species. Prohibited to fish for, retain, or land in EU waters. Assessed as Critically Endangered by IUCN.

name: Longnosed Skate
description: A skate species found in deep waters. Vulnerable to overfishing due to slow growth and late maturity.

name: Norwegian Skate
description: Norwegian skate are an EU Prohibited Species. Avoid eating.

name: White Skate
description: White skate are an EU Prohibited Species. Avoid eating.

name: Smoothhound
description: One of few shark species whose numbers appear to be stable. Their relatively high productivity means sustainable harvest is possible.

name: Dover Sole
description: The best choices are from the north Celtic Sea, the Bristol Channel and the western English Channel.

name: Lemon Sole
description: Best dusted in flour, fried in butter and eaten on the bone. Belongs to the same family as halibut and plaice.

name: Sand Sole
description: A flatfish species found in sandy-bottomed coastal waters of the northeastern Atlantic.

name: Sprat
description: Sprat are a highly resilient species and small artisanal inshore fisheries are unlikely to impact significantly on wider stocks.

name: Spurdog / Spiny Dogfish
description: Long-lived, slow growing with a high age at maturity. The Northeast Atlantic stock is depleted. Critically Endangered by IUCN.

name: Sturgeon
description: Sturgeons are greatly depleted and many species are in rapid decline. They are long-lived and slow to mature.

name: Swordfish
description: A magnificent solitary predator, extremely fast swimming with a sword-like bill. Can reach up to 4.5m in length!

name: Tilapia
description: Tilapia are omnivores with a low requirement for fishmeal, making them net producers of fish protein.

name: Rainbow Trout
description: Rainbow trout is the predominant farmed trout species. Rainbow trout farmed in freshwater is a good choice.

name: Albacore Tuna
description: Albacore are a moderate sized tuna primarily sold as fresh or frozen steaks and can also be used raw as sashimi.

name: Atlantic Bluefin Tuna
description: Vulnerable, slow growing and long lived. The market value of individual fish regularly reaches tens of thousands of pounds.

name: Bigeye Tuna
description: A relatively large species of tuna, able to tolerate colder waters and commonly found at greater depths.

name: Pacific Bluefin Tuna
description: Pacific bluefin continues to be subject to heavy overfishing and remains at or near historical lowest levels.

name: Skipjack Tuna
description: A relatively small tuna growing to a metre in length. Primarily sold in cans.

name: Southern Bluefin Tuna
description: Southern bluefin remains listed as Critically Endangered by the IUCN. Avoid eating.

name: Yellowfin Tuna
description: A big bulky tuna found in tropical or subtropical climates. The tail and some fins are yellow, the rest a glistening dark blue.

name: Turbot
description: Turbot is a valuable bycatch species. It is not subject to overfishing, and is not in an overfished state.

name: Tusk
description: Deepsea fish highly vulnerable to over-exploitation with low resilience to fishing. Avoid eating.

name: Whiting
description: Whiting are mainly a bycatch species with high discard rates. More selective fishing gears required.

name: Witch Flounder
description: Fisheries for witch in EU waters are unregulated. Generally taken as bycatch in trawls targeting whitefish.

name: Wolffish
description: Slow growing fish, vulnerable to overfishing. There is no stock assessment in EU waters. Avoid eating.

name: Ballan Wrasse
description: A colorful wrasse species found in rocky coastal waters of the northeastern Atlantic.

name: Wreckfish
description: A large deep-water fish found in temperate and tropical oceans worldwide.
